Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-04-28 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Zoom link: (redacted)
Recordings: cloud.fireflies.link/fg-20270428-rg (note: auto-caption)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Asha Kapoor (VP Eng, RiverGate), Tom Reynolds (SRE), Diego Marquez (ML Eng), Priya Singh (Product)

Optional auto-sections (auto-generated):
Summary: High-level discovery focused on p95 latency targets for streaming conversational agent and throughput for batch summarization/batching. Customer is evaluating hosted first but wants a clear path to Dedicated or Private (V P C) for compliance and cost at scale. Decided to run a three-profile benchmark and exchange traffic traces.
Topics: p95 targets, concurrency profiles, streaming token/sec, cold-starts, KV cache behavior, VPC/private deployment constraints, SOC 2 & KMS, Canary/fallbacks.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE on the account, and Liam is our solutions engineer. Quick agenda: hear about your workload and constraints, p95 goals, and then talk through hosted vs dedicated vs private options and benchmarking.
[00:18] Asha (RiverGate): Hi, thanks. We're looking to add an in-chat route summarization and a streaming assistant that can join live dispatch conversations. Our key metric is p95 token latency under streaming loads. We want <200ms p95 for short responses (10-40 tokens) and under 500ms for longer streams up to 200 tokens, with burst concurrency up to roughly 120 concurrent streams during peak.
[00:40] Liam (Redwood SE): Cool. When you say "burst" is that sustained for minutes or seconds? Does it have a ramp profile?
[00:48] Tom (SRE): Typically spikes last 3-8 minutes and come in waves, but sometimes we see a 20-30 minute plateau during incidents. Our 95th percentile target is what the product team needs for SLAs.
[01:05] Diego (ML Eng): Also important: we do batching for nightly summarization, about 3k requests in a batch window, and want tokens/sec metrics for throughput planning — approximately 40-60 tokens/sec per GPU for our benchmark model if we quantize.
[01:28] Maya: Good, that gives us two workloads: streaming low-latency at concurrency and batch high-throughput. For hosted, we can typically meet sub-200ms p95 for small payloads on optimized streaming paths depending on model choice and kernel selection. For the bigger 200-token responses 500ms maybe tight; we'd look at dedicated capacity or auto-burst options. Note: some transcriptions may show product names slightly off — e.g., Redwood Dedicated sometimes shown as "Reedwood Dedication" in auto captions.
[01:56] Asha: We have strict audit and encryption rules — SOC 2 is required, and we need KMS integration and audit logs retained for 13 months. Also SSO + SAML, RBAC, and ability to pin a model version.
[02:12] Liam: All supported. Private deployment gives you customer-controlled K M S and can be air-gapped if needed; Dedicated gives isolated pools and configurable autoscaling; Hosted is the fastest path but we'll need to discuss data retention and encryption at rest.
[02:30] Priya (Product): From product we care about graceful degradation — if we lose dedicated pool capacity, can we fallback to a cheaper hosted variant?
[02:39] Liam: Yes, smart routing with fallback to a compatible model variant is standard. We'll define fallbacks and fail-open vs fail-closed policies in the rollout.
[02:48] Tom: For our benchmarking we want end-to-end numbers, including network latencies from our edge to your hosted region. We also want cold start times measured for first token on a warmed vs cold KV cache.
[03:05] Diego: Quick question — how does Redwood manage KV cache invalidation for streaming sessions? We've seen weird growth in kv entries when clients reconnect.
[03:14] Liam: Good call — runtime keeps a per-session KV cache; reconnect semantics depend on session id reuse. We can evict older sessions after TTL and provide cache metrics. In some logs auto-transcription shows KV as "K V cash" which is weird but yes it's the same cache concept.
[03:33] Asha: Pricing is a concern. We are cost sensitive, especially with a high token volume for our nightly batches. If dedicated is more expensive up-front, can you show cost per 1M tokens for hosted vs dedicated amortized with reserved capacity?
[03:46] Maya: We'll send a cost model. For reference, typical hosted per-token numbers vary by model and streaming vs non-streaming; Dedicated gives better unit economics at scale, we'll include reserved commit scenarios.
[04:02] [04:02] Tom (SRE): Also region; our EU customers need data residency. Do you have EU hosted regions with the same performance?
[04:10] Liam: Yes, we have region parity in EU and NA. For Private deployments we can support on-prem or V P C peering into your cloud region for strict residency.
[04:22] Asha: For the p95 targets, we need to be specific about payload profiling: typical prompt is 80 tokens input, expect ~120 tokens output; streaming will the tokens/sec be stable?
[04:34] Liam: Streaming throughput depends on model size, quantization, and batching. On an optimized runtime, a 7B-ish quantized model might yield 40-60 tokens/sec on a T4-equivalent or higher; larger models lower. We'll run tests with your model or a closest open model.
[04:50] Diego: We do use some in-house finetuned LLaMA variant; can you run benchmarks against that?
[04:55] Liam: We can run bench runs in our sandbox with your artifact (S3 link or container). Need to discuss licensing and transfer — for Private you can keep it inside your V P C.
[05:06] Maya: Let's sketch the benchmark plan now so everyone is aligned. Proposed three profiles:
- Profile A: Streaming low-latency — 10-40 token answers, p95 target <200ms, concurrency 0-120 with 30s average session length.
- Profile B: Streaming long-form — 200-token outputs, p95 target <500ms, concurrency 0-60 sustained for 10+ minutes.
- Profile C: Batch summarization — 3k requests in batch, maximize tokens/sec and overall throughput; cost per 1M tokens.
[05:35] Priya: That maps to our internal categories. Also include cold-start tests: spin up new model instance and measure first-token latency under load.
[05:44] Liam: Will do. Also plan to capture p50/p90/p95/p99 and token/sec, GPU utilization, and tail latencies. We'll provide a spreadsheet template — shared link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/rg-bench-template (placeholder).
[06:00] Asha: Security checklist — SOC 2 report, encryption at rest, SAML SSO, audit logs, customer-managed keys — please send docs.
[06:09] Maya: We'll attach our security pack (SOC2, ISO references, KMS integration guide). Note the filename in my notes is "redwood-security-pack-2027.pdf".
[06:17] Tom: One more question on canarying — we want canary deploys and automatic fallback if p95 crosses threshold. How fine-grained are routing policies?
[06:27] Liam: You can do percent-based rollouts, route by customer tier, and set automatic rollback policies tied to telemetry thresholds. Our console supports per-route SLO alerts.
[06:36] Diego: For measuring token/sec, do you measure tokens emitted by model or tokens delivered over the stream including protocol overhead? We need consistent definitions.
[06:45] Liam: We'll measure model-emitted tokens at runtime and give network-level tokens/sec including latency; we'll clarify definitions in the runbook to avoid confusion.
[06:55] [07:00] Maya: Alright, any blockers to sending over the traces?
[07:04] Tom: We'll anonymize and deliver a 7-day trace. One note: sometimes our load patterns include sudden 10x spikes for a brief 30 seconds — please include a stress test scenario.
[07:16] Liam: We'll include a "token storm" stress profile. For Dedicated, if you reserve capacity we can also enable burst buffers to absorb short spikes.
[07:27] Asha: If we go Private, what's the expected lead time for on-prem or V P C deployment?
[07:33] Maya: Private lead time is typically 6-12 weeks depending on procurement and networking. Dedicated is faster — days to weeks for reserved pools. Hosted is immediate.
[07:44] Priya: Who will be our day-to-day contact on the engineering side for runbook and benchmarks?
[07:49] Maya: Liam will lead the technical bench work and I'll coordinate procurement and pricing.
[07:55] [08:00] Liam: Quick architecture rec: runtime does automatic batching when possible, but for streaming we do continuous token generation with optimized kernels; KV cache is per-session, and cache warming matters for p95 on the first tokens.
[08:15] Diego: How do you handle multiplexing across tenants on hosted GPUs? We need isolation guarantees for noisy neighbors.
[08:21] Liam: Hosted uses multi-tenant lanes with QoS scheduling; Dedicated gives assigned pools to you, which is better for guarantees. If you need single-tenant GPUs we can explore Dedicated single-tenant or Private.
[08:34] Asha: Regarding observability, we want token-level tracing and per-request breakdown of latency (model compute vs network vs queue).
[08:41] Liam: Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdown, per-route dashboards, and we can add tracing hooks for your org to ingest into our tracing or export to your system.
[08:53] Maya: Quick check — are there any blockers around compliance or procurement?
[08:58] Asha: Procurement will need enterprise terms for Dedicated/Private. Also legal will check data residency clauses if we move to hosted.
[09:06] Maya: Understood, we'll surface legal standard terms and enterprise addenda.
[09:12] [09:15] (15-minute summary skipped in auto transcript)
[24:20] Liam: Real-world note — we often see p95 improvements by enabling KV cache affinity and minor prompt engineering to reduce token churn. Also quantization options can improve tokens/sec but may change quality; we'll include quality regressions in the eval.
[24:40] Diego: We'll want an automated quality check — run eval sets in parallel to bench runs and check for hallucination/regression.
[24:47] Liam: Yes, Redwood Optimize has suggestions and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. We'll incorporate a QA step.
[25:05] Asha: Any specific hardware recommendations? We're cloud-agnostic but leaning to NVIDIA H-series for dedicated.
[25:12] Liam: H-series or A-series recommended for larger models; for quantized 7b/13b mixes, A100 or H100-like perf helps but cost increases. We'll recommend a profile in the runbook.
[25:27] Priya: Let's talk timeline for the pilot — we want to run bench in staging next month and decide by mid-May.
[25:35] Maya: Sounds good. Proposed calendar: bench kickoff 2027-05-06, deliverables 2 weeks for initial report, then decision meeting 2027-05-20.
[25:46] Tom: We'll try to get the trace to you by 2027-05-06.
[25:50] Maya: Great. I'll send calendar invites and the pricing sheet.
[25:56] [End wrap-up]
[25:58] Maya: Recap — (1) Redwood to send pricing + security pack, (2) Liam to draft benchmarking runbook and sheet, (3) RiverGate to provide traces and model artifact access or sample prompts. We'll run three profiles including a token-storm stress test.
[26:20] Asha: That works. Thanks everyone.
